calibration: Phrase matching is useful for discovery but over-reports generic nouns and can select a semantically wrong target when a phrase is overloaded across domains. A candidate should be accepted only when expanding the target answers a concrete question raised by that exact sentence. Existing links should not be repeated in later explanatory prose, and a prerequisite list does not require every occurrence of its name to be linked. In this shard, the strongest corrections were context-specific links to domain, trace, holomorphicity, Cauchy integral formula, identity theorem, uniformly bounded family, series, interval, and neighborhood. No independent missing definition or missing dependency was confirmed.
